# Experimental CACHE.JLM
Separate diagnostic prototype, never part of the baseline build or boot profile. Device ID FD05 is provisional and must be checked against the complete loaded JLM set before use. V86 only. AX=0 ping returns AX=1 BX=FD05; AX=1 writes a 160-byte conventional-memory buffer (ES:DI). Status 0 success, 1 invalid pointer, 6 unsupported CPU/op. Fixed whitelist of Intel family 6 models 5/6/7/8/A/B with CPUID MSR+MTRR support. No arbitrary register selectors, writes to MSRs, cache policy changes, page table changes, or hardware I/O.

Layout (little endian): u32 ABI 0x10000, signature, feature EDX, captured variable count (max 8), u64 MTRRCAP, u64 DEF_TYPE, then eight pairs of u64 PHYSBASE/PHYSMASK. Count can be smaller than hardware count. This does NOT report PAT/PTE mapping type, fixed MTRRs, or effective cache policy. No claim that the framebuffer is WC. Raw MSRs are intentionally retained for offline interpretation.

Build explicitly with sh diagnostics/cache/build.sh in the existing NASM/OpenWatcom environment. Unlike the 386 baseline, this isolated diagnostic includes runtime-gated CPUID/RDMSR; no purity exemptions were added to production builds. No automatic loading. No fault handler for hypervisor/firmware MSR traps; do not load on unsupported or unqualified systems. Requires review of DDB ID, JEMM caller context, privilege/fault handling, assembler/linker output and actual hardware validation before use. Prototype only.
